title: El Animo
label: ch:es-animo
canDo: I can say what is going on inside me: what hurts, what I care about, what I am struggling to do, and what I wish I had not done.

payoff.summary: Read the message or notice this chapter's words exist for, then say the same thing back.
payoff.note: Wordlist derived from the A2 mock audit by the solo-blocker rule described on chapter 440. THE CHAPTER TEACHES NO NEW GRAMMAR, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN: five words are handed to two machines the learner already owns. The thing-is-the-subject machine from gustar (chapter 35) takes doler and interesar -- 'me duele la cabeza', 'me interesan los cursos', where the verb agrees with the body part or the courses and never with the person, which is the commonest English-speaker error because English puts the person in charge. The reflexive from equivocarse (437) takes acercarse, concentrarse and arrepentirse, and 'se acerca la fecha' extends it: nobody moves the date, so the reflexive marks NO AGENT NAMED rather than did-it-to-itself. interesar is the verb behind ES-C398-interesante, which the learner already has -- the same free move as concierto -> concertar in 442. THE PIVOT IS ARREPENTIRSE, the sharpest trap in the tranche: it looks like a- + re- + sentir and is a- + re- + paenitere, AND IT CONJUGATES LIKE SENTIR (me arrepiento, nos arrepentimos), so the form misleads and the behaviour agrees with the form. Both are accidents of shape -- any verb with a stressed stem e breaks that way, related or not. Harder than 438's reir, where taking re- off left nothing; here it leaves pentir, which stands on nothing, and the only reason to think otherwise is the resemblance. A resemblance is not evidence.
